history.period: Ancient (mythological origin; no documented construction date)
history.summary: Major Shakti Peetha atop Purnagiri hill (also called Punyagiri, 'mountain of good deeds') at ~910 m, about 20-21 km from Tanakpur in Champawat district, near the India-Nepal border on the Kali (Sharda) River. Hindu legend says the navel (nabhi) of Goddess Sati fell here during Shiva's tandava; counted among the 51 Shakti Peethas (some sources say 108 Siddha Peethas). The temple is reached via road to Thulligad/Thuniyas and a 3 km paved staircase trek; free dharmashala lodging is available at the shrine. CSV town/state correction: CSV gives 'Champawat' (which is the district); the actual nearest town is Tanakpur, and the state is Uttarakhand.

name: Purnagiri Temple
town_description: Tanakpur is a gateway town in Champawat district, Uttarakhand, on the banks of the Kali (Sharda) River near the India-Nepal border. It has its own railway station and is the base for the Purnagiri pilgrimage.

travel.railway: Tanakpur Railway Station (town has its own station)
travel.road: Road from Tanakpur to Thulligad (~17-20 km), then a 3 km paved staircase trek to the temple

visitor_information.best_time: October to May; peak during Chaitra Navratri (March-April) for the Purnagiri Mela
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM generally; reported open round the clock during peak Navratri season (verify locally)
